summary.text: A 16-year-old woman visited an outpatient clinic with rapid enlargement of a large left breast mass over 12 months. Examination showed a huge mass occupying the lower quadrants of the left breast with expansion of the overlying skin and nipple areolar complex, and the authors describe her breast asymmetry. Ultrasonography showed a lobulated, well-circumscribed solid mass.

Fine-needle aspiration and Tru-Cut needle biopsies were consistent with a benign phyllodes tumor. After careful discussion of tumor access and the excess skin envelope, a periareolar mastopexy approach was planned, and preoperative markings were measured against the normal contralateral breast dimensions.

In a single-stage periareolar mastopexy, the skin between the circles was deepithelialized, the tumor was widely excised through the lower half of the outer periareolar incision, the parenchyma was fixed to the pectoralis fascia, and a round block suture closed the skin. The removed tumor was a well-encapsulated lobulated fibrous mass of 12 cm, histopathologically a benign phyllodes tumor without obvious mitosis or cellular atypia.

Three months postoperatively, the symmetry of both breasts was nearly identical in nipple-areola complex position, skin quality and breast shape, and the figure caption states that breast symmetry and projection had been restored.
